messages:
Ravi N.: Heads up — I hit an import failure trying to run the TypeScript sample on Bun and Cloudflare Pages. Error: "SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'" when importing 'redwood' from the node_modules bundle.
Elena K.: Bun/Pages expect ESM. Is our package.json publishing the correct conditional exports?
Ravi N.: package.json exports currently: ```json
{"exports": {".": {"require": "./dist/redwood.cjs", "import": "./dist/redwood.mjs", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"}, "./*": "./dist/*"}}
```
Tom B.: That looks right but some bundlers ignore conditional exports or resolve via entrypoint + package.json "type" field. What's our "type" set to?
Ravi N.: It's "commonjs" for now to preserve older Node consumers. That might be the issue. Bun sees package as cjs and treats dist files differently.
Ivy Z.: We can't flip type to module without breaking CJS consumers. Options: 1) keep "type": "commonjs" but ensure top-level "exports" has explicit string mappings for subpaths including "./package.json" and "./types"; 2) publish a separate "browser" field or a tiny ESM-only package under @redwood/web where edge users can opt-in; 3) use conditional exports with an `"node": {"import":..., "require":...}` and `"worker": "./dist/redwood.worker.mjs"` condition for edge.
Elena K.: I like the worker condition idea. Does Node's resolver support custom conditions? Not broadly. But bundlers (esbuild/rollup) allow custom conditions. We can add a `"worker"` condition and document it for edge consumers; then sample apps can set `conditions: ['worker']` in their bundler when building.
Ravi N.: short-term fix: add an `exports['./browser']` -> `./dist/redwood.browser.mjs` and update the sample-app to import 'redwood/browser' for edge demos.
Tom B.: Also add a `types` conditional export per path to avoid TS falling back to the wrong d.ts. Example: ```json
"exports": {".": {"require": "./dist/redwood.cjs","import": "./dist/redwood.mjs","types": "./dist/index.d.ts"},"./browser": {"import": "./dist/redwood.browser.mjs","types": "./dist/index.browser.d.ts"},"./*": "./dist/*"}
``` 
Ivy Z.: We'll need CI matrix to smoke test: node-cjs, node-esm, bun, deno, worker. I'll add a GH Action matrix. Also create a simple TS devcontainer that reproduces the Bun import error.
CI Bot: Created canary release `redwood@edge-smoke-202603` and queued sample-app edge smoke job.
Ravi N.: Verified canary on Bun — sample builds and runs in Pages preview. :tada: Filing follow-ups: 1) RFC for long-term dual package strategy (single package vs split ESM-only package); 2) small runtime guard message for CJS->ESM mismatch; 3) update onboarding docs and sample-app to clearly show edge import path.
Elena K.: Great, let's keep the RFC minimal — pros/cons, migration path, telemetry to know how many CJS users remain. 
Tom B.: I'll add the d.ts per subpath generation to the build pipeline too.
Ivy Z.: Thanks team. Once RFC lands, we can schedule a quick office hours to walk through migration guidance.
